title: Take As Many Courses As Possible Before Their Deadlines

concept.title: Go by deadline; when time runs out, throw away the longest course taken so far
body: A course takes `duration` days and must be **finished** by its `deadline` (on or before that day). Courses are taken one after another, starting on day 1, with no overlap. What is the **largest number of courses** that can be completed?

Process the courses in order of **deadline**, and keep the courses taken so far. Add the new course (its duration goes to the total time). If the total time now exceeds the new deadline, the schedule is broken: drop one of the courses taken, and the best one to drop is the **longest** one, because it frees the most time and costs only one course (the count goes back to what it was). A **max-heap of durations** finds the longest course.

body.code:
courses.sort(key=lambda c: c[1])        # by deadline
heap, time = [], 0
for duration, deadline in courses:
    time += duration
    heappush(heap, -duration)           # max-heap of durations
    if time > deadline:
        time += heappop(heap)           # drop the longest course (its duration is negative here)
print(len(heap))

body: Why does it work? After each step the heap holds the **largest set** of courses (among the first ones by deadline) that can be finished, and among such sets the one with the **smallest total time**; a smaller total time is only better for the courses that come later. The dropped course may be the new course itself, which is fine. The total time can reach 2 * 10^13, so use 64-bit integers.

statement: There are `n` courses. Course `i` takes `duration` days and must be finished on or before the day `deadline`. You take the courses one after another, starting on day 1, with no gaps needed and no overlap (a course that starts after `t` days of work ends on the day `t + duration`). Print the largest number of courses that you can take.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`, the number of courses.
Each of the next `n` lines has two numbers: the `duration` of a course and its `deadline`.
outputFormat: Print the maximum number of courses.

examples.note: Take the courses with the durations 100, 1000 and 200 in the order of their deadlines (200, 1250, 1300): they end on the days 100, 1100 and 1300. The fourth course (2000 days) does not fit: 3.

hints: Sort the courses by deadline and add them one by one.
Keep the durations of the taken courses in a max-heap and the total time.
If the total time exceeds the current deadline, remove the longest course from the heap and subtract its duration.

explanation: Courses are added in order of deadline; a max-heap holds the durations of the courses taken. When the total time exceeds the current deadline, the longest course is dropped. The heap size is the answer.
solution.complexity: Time O(n log n), space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
c = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]

import heapq
c.sort(key=lambda course: course[1])
heap = []
time = 0
for duration, deadline in c:
    time += duration
    heapq.heappush(heap, -duration)
    if time > deadline:
        time += heapq.heappop(heap)
print(len(heap))
